findings.title: Format/String mutates receiver for negative durations, so a second call gives a wrong result
findings.property: Formatting the same *Durafmt twice returns the same string, and Duration() is unchanged by formatting
findings.actual: first call "-1 microsecond", second call "-"; Duration() returns +1µs after formatting (d.duration = -d.duration is written back to the receiver while d.input still starts with '-')
findings.evidence: Format is a pure formatting method (String() is also used by fmt via Stringer, and Duration() is a getter); the code negates d.duration in place at durafmt.go:94 whenever input[0]=='-', so each call flips the sign again and formatting has side effects.

error.message: String() not repeatable: first "-1 microsecond", second "-"

review.title: Format/String negates d.duration in place for negative durations, so repeated calls give wrong output
review.reason: durafmt.go:94 does `d.duration = -d.duration` on the receiver whenever input starts with '-', but input is never changed. The first call leaves the stored duration positive, and the second call negates it back to negative, so the unit calculations run on a negative value and the output collapses to "-". Nothing in the docs or tests suggests this is intentional. A pure formatter should be repeatable, and `Duration()` should not change after formatting. The fix is a one-line change to use a local copy of the duration, and a maintainer would take it.

fix.reason: the repro passes on the patched code
